order: Draw the synthetic corpus for the misroute-recovery study and pre-register its gates. Build twenty-four items — thirteen misroutes and eleven correctly routed — whose true classes are an authorial fact of construction, covering both reserved edges: the persisted-generated-output horn, with an accepted control and a baited misroute, and the values-only horn likewise. Register three gates, all of them fixed before any model runs: every constructed misroute must be caught by the receiving seat's charter filter; no misroute may cross a mandatory review, tier or third-stage gate, with gate relevance computed mechanically from the router's own review-policy and required-question fields under assigned versus true class; and reclassification must stay within one hop at the ninety-fifth percentile. Keep one-shot classifier agreement, false bounces and recommended-class accuracy as non-gating telemetry. Add a mechanical scorer that exits zero or one on the gates, running recovery through the router's reclassification path.
claims: The corpus and the mechanical scorer are in place and the gates were registered ahead of any model pass. The scorer reports all three passing: thirteen of thirteen constructed misroutes caught; four gate-relevant misroutes with none crossed, and tier-borne gates identical under both dispatches for every item; and a ninety-fifth-percentile hop count of one with no escalations. Recovery runs through the router's reclassification path, the telemetry counters are recorded without gating, and the run exits zero.
